topIssues.title: kona: MessageGraph uses hardcoded MESSAGE_EXPIRY_WINDOW instead of dependency set config
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
## Description

Kona's `MessageGraph` in `rust/kona/crates/protocol/interop/src/graph.rs` (line ~180) uses a hardcoded `MESSAGE_EXPIRY_WINDOW` constant (7 days) when checking message expiry. It does not read the configurable message expiry window from the dependency set.

This means the fault proof program (kona) cannot detect expired messages when the dependency set has a custom (shorter) expiry window configured, even though the supernode and challenger trace provider correctly use the dependency set's value.

## Impact

The `TestInteropFaultProofs_MessageExpiry` acceptance test cannot run its FPP subtests because the test configures a 10-second expiry window via `WithMessageExpiryWindow(10)`, but kona still uses the 7-day hardcoded constant and doesn't detect the expiry.

## Expected behavior

Kona should read the message expiry window from the dependency set configuration (passed via rollup configs or the preimage oracle) rather than using a hardcoded constant.

## References

- Hardcoded constant: `rust/kona/crates/protocol/interop/src/graph.rs` ~line 180
- Acceptance test skip: `op-acceptance-tests/tests/superfaultproofs/superfaultproofs.go` in `RunMessageExpiryTest`

topIssues.title: op-chain-ops: update check super root script to work with super node
topIssues.author: stevennevins
topIssues.body:
The verification script that we have used previously to verify that a SuperRoot was valid needs to be updated to work with SuperNode 

We need to update the inputs to use a SuperNode RPC for the dependency set.

And remove the need to pass each chain RPC for the dependency set.


Old API

```
go run op-chain-ops/cmd/check-super-root/main.go --rpc-endpoints $RPC_URL_1,$RPC_URL_2 --timestamp $SUPER_ROOT_TIMESTAMP
go run op-chain-ops/cmd/check-super-root/main.go --rpc-endpoints $RPC_URL_1,$RPC_URL_2
```

New API

```
go run op-chain-ops/cmd/check-super-root/main.go --super-node-rpc $SUPER_NODE_RPC --timestamp $SUPER_ROOT_TIMESTAMP
go run op-chain-ops/cmd/check-super-root/main.go --super-node-rpc $SUPER_NODE_RPC
```

topPRs.title: op-deployer: remove RPC deps via JSON-RPC replay proxy
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Introduces a JSON-RPC Replay Proxy that records Sepolia RPC request/response pairs to fixture files during development, then replays them offline in CI. This removes the `SEPOLIA_RPC_URL` dependency from ~16 op-deployer test cases.

### What Changed

**New files:**
- `op-service/testutils/devnet/rpcreplay.go` — RPCReplayProxy with record/replay modes, batch support, deterministic request keying
- `op-service/testutils/devnet/rpcreplay_test.go` — Unit tests for the proxy
- `op-service/testutils/devnet/fixtures/` — Directory for committed fixture files

**Modified files:**
- `op-service/testutils/devnet/canned.go` — Added helper functions: `RPCReplayOrRecord`, `NewForkedSepoliaFromBlockWithReplay`, `RPCReplayFixturePath`
- `op-deployer/pkg/deployer/pipeline/init_test.go` — 9 test functions: replaced `RetryProxy` + `SEPOLIA_RPC_URL` with replay proxy
- `op-deployer/pkg/deployer/integration_test/cli/upgrade_test.go` — 6 test cases: replaced `NewForkedSepoliaFromBlock` with `NewForkedSepoliaFromBlockWithReplay`
- `op-deployer/pkg/deployer/opcm/dispute_game_factory_test.go` — 1 test function: replaced direct `rpc.Dial(SEPOLIA_RPC_URL)` with replay proxy

### How It Works

The replay proxy is an HTTP server that sits between tests and Sepolia:

1. **Record mode** (`SEPOLIA_RPC_URL=<url> RPC_REPLAY_RECORD=true`): Forwards requests to real Sepolia, saves request/response pairs to a JSON fixture file keyed by `sha256(method + canonical_params)`
2. **Replay mode** (no `SEPOLIA_RPC_URL`): Serves responses from fixture files, no network calls
3. **Pass-through mode** (`SEPOLIA_RPC_URL=<url>` without `RPC_REPLAY_RECORD`): Forwards and records (useful for updating fixtures)

### Decisions Made

- **One fixture file per test function** — Each test gets its own fixture file to keep recordings isolated and debuggable
- **Deterministic keying** — `method:sha256(method+params)[:16]` ensures the same RPC call always maps to the same cache entry
- **ID stripping** — JSON-RPC `id` is stripped from cached responses and reconstructed on replay, so different request IDs don't cause cache misses
- **Batch support** — The proxy handles JSON-RPC batch requests (array of requests) correctly

### Complexity Report

- **Moderate complexity** — The proxy itself is straightforward (~300 lines). The main work was updating 16 test cases across 3 files.
- **Key risk**: Fixture files need to be generated before CI can run in replay mode. This PR sets up the infrastructure but **fixture files are not yet generated** — that requires a one-time recording pass with `SEPOLIA_RPC_URL` set.
- **Anvil interaction**: For `upgrade_test.go`, anvil makes its own RPC calls to the fork URL. The replay proxy sits between anvil and Sepolia, intercepting all those calls.

### Side Effects

- No version bumps needed
- No snapshot changes
- Test behavior is identical when `SEPOLIA_RPC_URL` is set (backward compatible)

### Next Steps

1. Run tests with `SEPOLIA_RPC_URL` set + `RPC_REPLAY_RECORD=true` to generate fixture files
2. Commit the generated fixture files
3. Verify tests pass without `SEPOLIA_RPC_URL` (replay mode)

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for RPCReplayProxy (record/replay/batch/deterministic keys)
- [ ] Record fixtures with real Sepolia RPC
- [ ] Verify all 16 test cases pass in replay mode
- [ ] Verify CI passes without SEPOLIA_RPC_URL

topPRs.title: feat(contracts): add ProxyAdminOwnedBase to L2 proxied contracts with initialize()
topPRs.author: maurelian
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Moves `ProxyAdminOwnedBase` from `src/L1/` to `src/universal/` so it can be used by both L1 and L2 contracts
- Adds `ProxyAdminOwnedBase` inheritance to 7 L2 contracts that have `initialize()` functions, matching the pattern already used by L1 contracts
- Each initializer now calls `_assertOnlyProxyAdminOrProxyAdminOwner()` as its first statement to gate re-initialization behind proxy admin ownership

**Contracts updated (have `initialize()`):**
- `FeeVault` (covers `BaseFeeVault`, `L1FeeVault`, `OperatorFeeVault`, `SequencerFeeVault` transitively)
- `L2CrossDomainMessenger`
- `L2StandardBridge` (covers `L2StandardBridgeInterop` transitively)
- `L2ERC721Bridge`
- `FeeSplitter`
- `LiquidityController`
- `OptimismMintableERC721Factory`

**Contracts intentionally excluded:**
- Contracts without `initialize()` — inheritance would be unused dead code
- `OptimismSuperchainERC20` — BeaconProxy instances, incompatible with `ProxyAdminOwnedBase`

**`L2Genesis.s.sol` changes to support the new assertion:**
- `_setImplementationCode` now calls `EIP1967Helper.setAdmin(impl, Predeploys.PROXY_ADMIN)` so impl addresses pass the `proxyAdmin()` check
- `setPredeployImplementations` pranks as `opChainProxyAdminOwner` so the ownership assertion passes during genesis
- `setL2ProxyAdmin` moved to run first so `proxyAdminOwner()` is set before other contracts' initializers check it

## Test plan

- [ ] `FOUNDRY_PROFILE=lite forge test --match-path "test/L2/*"` — 381 passed, 0 failed, 37 skipped

topPRs.title: feat: Implement L2 Dev Flags
topPRs.author: 0xiamflux
topPRs.body:
## Overview
                                                                                                                                                       
  Added L2DevFeatureFlags predeploy at 0x420...002d that stores a per-chain dev feature bitmap, enabling L2CM to gate predeploy upgrades behind feature flags.

## Changes:
  - New L2DevFeatureFlags — stores bitmap in a custom storage slot.
  - Interop gating: 7 interop predeploys wrapped in if (_isDevFeatureEnabled(DevFeatures.OPTIMISM_PORTAL_INTEROP)) — when disabled, proxies are not upgraded.
  - L2CM upgrades the predeploy: L2CM now includes L2DevFeatureFlags in its upgrade flow.  
  - Genesis: `L2Genesis.setL2DevFeatureFlags()` deploys the impl and sets the bitmap at genesis via `DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT`.
